properties.cameraEngine_20260805: Rebuilt on @zxing/browser + @zxing/library (was html5-qrcode) per explicit user request. POSSIBLE_FORMATS restricted to retail 1D formats (EAN_13, EAN_8, UPC_A, UPC_E, CODE_128, CODE_39, ITF, CODABAR). Deliberately NOT using DecodeHintType.TRY_HARDER - see zxing_tryharder_bug node.
properties.strictModeRace_20260805: React 18 StrictMode's dev-mode double-effect-invoke was found causing two concurrent camera instances to write into the same DOM target, TWICE, in two different shapes: (1) with html5-qrcode, two <video> elements got appended into the same container div, visible as a doubled/frozen feed; (2) after switching to ZXing (which uses a React-owned <video> ref instead of a DOM-id string), ZXing's controls.stop() unconditionally clears the shared video element's srcObject (cleanVideoSource) - not scoped to 'its own' stream - so the two StrictMode phantom instances fought over the same element again, and whichever's delayed stop-cleanup fired last wiped out the other's already-working feed. Fixed with a teardownChainRef (a useRef holding a promise chain) that serializes start/stop across effect invocations - each new instance's startCamera() first awaits the PREVIOUS instance's full teardown promise before touching the shared video ref, guaranteeing no overlap regardless of StrictMode's double-invoke timing.
properties.scanBoxFix_20260805: The qrbox/scan-region was a small fixed 300x200px patch, centered in the frame - the decoder never even looks outside it. A user screenshot showed a real barcode sitting in the corner of frame, well outside the box, which is why it never detected despite being clearly visible. Changed to a function-based qrbox sized to ~90% of the actual video frame dimensions (html5-qrcode era) / equivalent framing guidance in the ZXing rebuild, making alignment far more forgiving.
properties.offlineDecodeProof_20260805: Proved the decode pipeline itself is correct independent of any camera/lighting variable: hand-built a bit-perfect, checksum-valid EAN-13 barcode bit pattern directly from the EAN-13 spec (@zxing/library has no built-in 1D encoder to auto-generate one - only QR/DataMatrix/Aztec writers are exported), fed it through the exact MultiFormatReader config the app uses (same hints, same format restriction), and it decoded correctly (frontend, node -e test, not committed as a test file). This isolates any remaining real-world scan failures to camera capture conditions (focus/lighting/distance/motion), not application code.
properties.beep: frontend/src/utils/beep.js - Web Audio API synthesized tone, no audio asset - plays on successful add-to-cart for both the camera-scan and hardware-scanner/manual-entry paths (POS.jsx handleScanned/handleBarcodeEnter)
properties.STATUS_NOT_YET_CONFIRMED: As of 2026-08-05, every known code-level bug has been found and fixed, and the decode logic is proven correct offline - but a live successful scan of a REAL physical barcode via the actual camera was never confirmed working by the user in this pass. properties.foundDuring: 2026-08-05 barcode scanner rebuild, while investigating console warnings during live camera testing
properties.bug: HTMLCanvasElementLuminanceSource.getTempCanvasElement() checks 'if (null === this.tempCanvasElement)' to lazily create a temp canvas, but the field is never initialized to null anywhere in the constructor - it's actually undefined. undefined !== null (strict equality), so the lazy-creation branch never executes, and rotate() immediately hits 'if (!tempCanvasElement) throw new Error("Could not create a Canvas element.")'. This fires on EVERY decode frame whenever DecodeHintType.TRY_HARDER is set, because TRY_HARDER is what triggers OneDReader's rotation-based retry path for 1D barcodes.
properties.verifiedNotFixedUpstream: Checked npm view @zxing/browser versions / @zxing/library versions - 0.2.1 and 0.23.0 respectively are the latest published releases as of 2026-08-05, so this is not an outdated-dependency problem; the bug is present in the current latest release.
properties.workaround: Simply don't set DecodeHintType.TRY_HARDER. Trade-off: TRY_HARDER is specifically meant to help recover marginal/blurry/rotated reads, which is exactly the kind of image quality problem a fixed-focus laptop webcam produces - so this is a real capability loss, not a free fix. Revisit if a future @zxing/browser release fixes the underlying field initialization.

nodes.label: WhatsApp phone number format bug (systemic, production-breaking)

properties.severity: Every phone number in the live database (shops.whatsapp_number, suppliers.phone, customers.phone) was stored in local Pakistani format (03001234567, what a shopkeeper actually types), but both wa.me deep-links and the WhatsApp Cloud API require full international format with no leading trunk zero (923001234567). Passing local format straight through made wa.me show 'phone number shared via url is invalid' and would make a real Cloud API send fail outright with the wrong 'to' field. This silently broke EVERY WhatsApp touchpoint (supplier orders, low-stock alerts, daily/weekly reports, subscription payment-proof links) for any shop using real (non-demo) phone numbers.
properties.fix: Added normalizePakistaniPhone() to backend/src/services/whatsappService.js, applied inside BOTH sendTextMessage() (Cloud API path) and buildWhatsAppUrl() (wa.me path). Also found and fixed a SECOND, duplicated, unnormalized phone-cleaning implementation that had drifted into shopController.js's requestSubscriptionUpgrade - replaced with a call to the same shared buildWhatsAppUrl().
properties.verified: Live: Suppliers page's supplier-order button now generates a correct wa.me/923001234567 link (was wa.me/03001234567 before, which WhatsApp rejects as invalid). Re-tested all three cron endpoints (low-stock/daily/weekly) against a shop with fully local-format numbers - zero errors, correct international-format numbers in every generated link. Full 48-test Jest suite still passing.

properties.foundDuring: An audit of delete capabilities across every entity (Products, Categories, Suppliers, Customers, Expenses, Sales, Purchases, Notifications), triggered by an unrelated user question about whether shop owners could delete their own test data.

properties.userRequest: User asked for the POS 'Scan' button to detect whether a hardware barcode scanner is connected and use it, showing a 'connect to Barcode Scanner' message if not - user shared a photo of their actual hardware (a handheld laser trigger-gun scanner and a Honeywell Orbit-style omnidirectional dome scanner).
properties.technicalConstraint: Both devices shown are standard USB/Bluetooth keyboard-emulation ('wedge') scanners in their default out-of-the-box mode - to the OS and browser they are INDISTINGUISHABLE from a keyboard. There is no web API that can detect 'is a keyboard-emulation device plugged in', since that's equivalent to asking 'is a keyboard plugged in', which no website can meaningfully answer. True connection detection only exists for a different, much rarer class of scanner exposing itself via WebHID/WebSerial with explicit per-device user permission - not what this user owns.
properties.decisionMade: Did NOT build a fake 'checking connection...' UI, since it would be non-functional/dishonest for this hardware. Built the real functional equivalent instead.
properties.fix: frontend/src/pages/dashboard/POS.jsx: search input (searchInputRef) now automatically regains focus via refocusSearch() after every action that could otherwise steal it - adding a product by clicking a card, closing the camera BarcodeScanner modal (both success and Cancel paths), and completing a checkout (clearCart()). Added a plain-language hint under the search bar explaining both paths. The existing handleBarcodeEnter (keydown-on-Enter) already handled the actual wedge-scanner input path from an earlier session - this fix is purely about making sure that input never loses focus mid-shift.

nodes.label: POS cart touch-target, alignment, scroll, and truncation fixes

properties.trigger: A sequence of user-reported bugs via screenshots/messages, each initially looking cosmetic but tracing back to distinct root causes.
properties.removeButtonBug: 'Remove doesn't work' turned out to be a working handler (removeFromCart) behind a 22x19px hit area - well under the ~44px touch-target guideline this phone-first POS needs. Enlarged .pos-remove-btn and .pos-qty-control button to 32x32px in frontend/src/pages/dashboard/POS.css.
properties.alignmentBugFirst: +/- glyphs looked vertically off next to a perfectly-centered x - .pos-qty-control button was missing the explicit display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center that .pos-remove-btn already had (plain text-centering in a button isn't reliable across different glyphs).
properties.scrollToTopBug: Clicking any product scrolled the whole page back to the top. Caused by an earlier-session feature (refocusSearch() for hardware wedge-scanner support) calling plain .focus() on the top-of-page search input after every addToCart() - browsers auto-scroll a newly-focused off-screen element into view by default. Fixed with searchInputRef.current?.focus({ preventScroll: true }) inside a requestAnimationFrame.
properties.alignmentBugSecond: A second, genuinely different misalignment: each .pos-cart-item row is its own independent CSS grid, so grid-template-columns: 1fr auto auto auto computed different column widths PER ROW based on that row's own price text (e.g. 'Rs 55' vs 'Rs 3600'), shifting qty/total/remove out of alignment across rows even though each button was internally centered correctly. Fixed by switching to fixed pixel columns (later trimmed to 1fr 92px 72px 32px) so every row shares identical column boundaries, like a real <table>.
properties.truncationAndScrollbarBug: Final screenshot showed 'Shan Birya...' cut off plus a stray icon next to the remove button. Only reproduced at 1000px width, where .pos-shell's 2-column desktop layout locks .pos-cart to a fixed 380px (confirmed via getComputedStyle - the name column was down to 99.2px). Fixed the name with a 2-line clamp (display:-webkit-box; -webkit-line-clamp:2) instead of single-line ellipsis, and trimmed the grid columns further to reclaim width. The 'stray icon' was the scrollbar's own arrow-button chrome (this browser/OS renders it) sitting directly on top of the remove-button column once the cart had enough items to scroll - fixed with padding-right: 0.5rem on .pos-cart-items.
properties.verified: Every fix confirmed live in-browser at the specific viewport/cart-size that reproduces it, not just visually - e.g. document.activeElement/window.scrollY checks for the scroll fix, getComputedStyle column-width checks for both alignment fixes, a real 3-item cart screenshot for the final truncation+scrollbar fix.

decisionLog.decision: Full backend migration MongoDB->Supabase Postgres per explicit user instruction ('shift backend A to Z to supabase, that's my final decision')
decisionLog.scope: Kept Express, JWT auth, and permission system unchanged - only the data layer moved. Zero frontend changes required.

decisionLog.decision: Used raw pg driver + parameterized SQL instead of Supabase JS client or an ORM (Prisma/Knex)
decisionLog.why: Supabase JS client goes through PostgREST, which only exposes the public schema by default (would need a Dashboard setting change I have no API access to). Raw pg avoids that limitation entirely and keeps transaction logic in JS, close to the original Mongoose session pattern.

decisionLog.decision: Created a dedicated 'retailpro' schema instead of using 'public'
decisionLog.why: This Supabase project already hosts an unrelated app with its own public.users table - collision risk. Checked via list_tables before writing any DDL.

decisionLog.decision: Must use Supabase pooler host (aws-0-<region>.pooler.supabase.com), never the direct db.<ref>.supabase.co host
decisionLog.why: Direct host is IPv6-only; most sandboxes/hosts have no outbound IPv6 route, connection times out with ENOTFOUND/ENODATA.

decisionLog.decision: FK constraints on *.product_id, purchases.supplier_id, sales.cashier_id are DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED
decisionLog.why: A full shop cascade-delete hits two independent FK paths (e.g. shops->products directly AND shops->sales->sale_items) with no ordering guarantee; RESTRICT (correct default) would block deletion of a row a not-yet-cascaded child still references. Deferring the check to commit time fixes this without weakening protection for an ordinary standalone delete.

decisionLog.decision: Registered a global pg type parser for NUMERIC (OID 1700) -> parseFloat
decisionLog.why: node-postgres returns NUMERIC as strings by default to avoid precision loss; every price/quantity field here is numeric(14,x) and the frontend does real arithmetic on these fields. Caught by 12 failing tests.

decisionLog.decision: Tests use a real isolated Postgres schema (retailpro_test) on the same Supabase project, not mocks or a different engine
decisionLog.why: Same reasoning as the original mongodb-memory-server choice - want the test suite to exercise the actual database engine, transactions, and constraints.

decisionLog.decision: Vercel deployment is blocked on Render backend deployment
decisionLog.why: Vercel only hosts the frontend; deploying it alone gives a URL with no working API behind it. User must complete the Render dashboard steps manually since there's no Render API access.

decisionLog.decision: Ruled out the deploy_to_vercel MCP tool (direct file upload, no git) for this project; use Vercel's dashboard Git import instead
decisionLog.why: That tool requires every source file embedded literally in the tool call. The frontend is 62 files / ~200KB even after excluding package-lock.json; a test read of the assembled payload alone hit ~113K tokens and got truncated by the Read tool's cap, confirming this path is impractical for a project this size (the tool's own description says it's meant for a small app just generated, not an existing multi-file repo). Git import is also strictly better long-term: auto-deploys on every future push, same pattern as Render.

decisionLog.decision: User pivoted backend deployment target from Render to Vercel Serverless, made directly (commit e837f35, not through an agent in this session)
decisionLog.why: Not stated in the commit; likely to keep both frontend and backend on one platform. Consequence flagged, not yet resolved: node-cron's WhatsApp scheduler (feature_whatsapp) has no persistent process to run on under serverless and will not fire. The pg.Pool's max:10 sizing is also tuned for a long-running server, not serverless cold starts. Both are open items - see deploy_vercel_backend node.

decisionLog.decision: User replaced native window.confirm() with a custom ConfirmModal component across all dashboard delete/remove actions (commit ce57f35)
decisionLog.why: window.confirm() is a jarring, unstyled native browser dialog that breaks the app's visual consistency; ConfirmModal matches the existing modal-overlay/modal-card pattern already used elsewhere (ProductFormModal, SimpleFormModal, StaffFormModal).

decisionLog.decision: Subscription billing built as a manual record-and-WhatsApp-ping flow, not a real payment gateway integration (commit 14629cf)
decisionLog.why: No JazzCash/EasyPaisa merchant API credentials/integration exist; local Pakistani retail SaaS commonly runs on manual bank-transfer + proof-of-payment. Flagged as a functional gap versus 'automated billing' - activateSubscription currently has no visible admin-only guard beyond the caller's own shopId, worth a security review before this is trusted as a real paywall.

decisionLog.decision: Added wa.me deep-links for supplier orders/low-stock instead of fixing the node-cron/serverless conflict (commit 67db8e7)
decisionLog.why: Cheapest way to keep WhatsApp usable given Vercel serverless can't run node-cron; trades automation for a manual click. The underlying scheduler problem (feature_whatsapp criticalCaveat) is still open, not resolved by this.

decisionLog.decision: Verified both Vercel deployments are actually live via direct HTTP checks, updated graph from 'not yet deployed' to confirmed-live
decisionLog.why: The graph had gone stale relative to the repo - PROJECT_PROGRESS.md and README already claimed live URLs but the machine-readable graph still said NOT YET DEPLOYED. Checked directly instead of trusting docs at face value.

decisionLog.decision: User asked to fix the two flagged weak areas (WhatsApp automation, subscription billing security) and add anything that would genuinely increase the product's market demand. Fixed both, plus added branches/transfers, thermal printing, and a payment provider scaffold.
decisionLog.why: Explicit user request: 'improve these things and take it to higher level, if adding something will improve the demand of this webapp then add it, if something is weaker than improve it.'

decisionLog.decision: Used the Supabase MCP tools (list_tables, execute_sql, apply_migration) to inspect and migrate the LIVE database directly, rather than only editing schema.sql and assuming it matched.
decisionLog.why: This is exactly what surfaced that schema.sql had drifted from the live DB (subscription_status/ends_at/last_payment_trx existed live but not in the DDL source) and that requestSubscriptionUpgrade was actually broken in production (notifications_type_check didn't allow 'subscription'). Reading the live schema first, rather than trusting the DDL file's own claim to be the source of truth, is what caught both.

decisionLog.decision: Scoped multi-branch as transfer-manifest tracking, not live per-branch inventory splitting
decisionLog.why: Splitting products.stock_quantity per branch would require rewriting the POS's SELECT...FOR UPDATE transactional stock-deduction path (saleController.js) - the single highest-risk, most load-bearing piece of the whole app. Chose the version that adds real value (a paper trail + workflow for multi-location shops, which is what the Enterprise tier's marketing copy already promises) without touching that code at all.

decisionLog.decision: Built a payment-provider scaffold for JazzCash/EasyPaisa instead of a fake 'live' integration
decisionLog.why: No real merchant credentials exist for this project, and guessing at JazzCash/EasyPaisa's actual API request/response field names from memory risked shipping code that looks like it works but silently fails against their real endpoints. Built the correct integration shape (isConfigured()/createPaymentRequest()) with a clear 'not configured, falls back to manual' error instead, so it's honest about what state it's in.

decisionLog.decision: Removed the self-service /api/shop/subscription/activate endpoint entirely rather than patching its permission check
decisionLog.why: Any check reachable via a shop owner's own JWT is fundamentally the wrong trust boundary for 'did this shop actually pay' - moved activation to a cross-tenant /api/admin/* surface gated by a separate secret (PLATFORM_ADMIN_KEY) the shop owner never has access to, rather than trying to find a permission flag that a compromised or dishonest owner couldn't also grant themselves.

decisionLog.decision: Switched the camera barcode scanner from html5-qrcode to @zxing/browser + @zxing/library on explicit user request ('use Zxing')
decisionLog.why: User asked directly. Recommended @zxing/browser specifically over any other option because html5-qrcode was already using a bundled/vendored copy of zxing-js internally with no direct configuration access - @zxing/browser is the actively-maintained official port, giving real control over format hints and the video element lifecycle (a React ref instead of a DOM-id string), which is what ended up mattering for the StrictMode bug fix.

decisionLog.decision: Removed DecodeHintType.TRY_HARDER from the barcode scanner instead of working around the upstream @zxing/browser bug some other way (e.g. patch-package)
decisionLog.why: The bug is in a third-party library's own uninitialized-field logic, not something reachable/fixable from application code without patching node_modules directly, which is fragile and would silently break again on any future dependency reinstall or version bump. Confirmed via npm view that 0.2.1/0.23.0 are the actual latest published releases, not a stale-install problem. Removing the hint trades away some real-world read robustness but ships a stable, non-crash-looping decode path today; documented clearly as an open item to revisit if upstream ever fixes it.

decisionLog.decision: Proved the ZXing decode pipeline correct via a hand-built synthetic EAN-13 image instead of only testing against the live camera
decisionLog.why: The live camera test kept failing for reasons that turned out to be either environmental (webcam focus/lighting, only the user can fix) or code bugs already found and fixed (StrictMode race, tiny scan box) - but without an independent, deterministic way to test the DECODE LOGIC alone (no camera, no lighting variable), it would have been impossible to tell 'is the code still broken' apart from 'is this just a hard physical scanning condition.' Building a real, checksum-valid barcode bit pattern by hand (no 1D encoder is exported from @zxing/library) and decoding it through the exact same MultiFormatReader config gave a clean, reproducible pass/fail signal independent of any physical camera.

decisionLog.decision: Did not build any 'is a barcode scanner connected' detection when the user asked for it, after confirming their hardware is a standard keyboard-emulation type
decisionLog.why: No web API can distinguish a keyboard-emulation HID device from an actual keyboard - building a fake detection UI would look like it works while never actually reflecting reality, which is worse than not having the feature at all. Explained the constraint plainly and built the real functional equivalent (never-losing-focus search input) instead of a dishonest approximation.

decisionLog.decision: Fixed WhatsApp phone number normalization at the shared whatsappService.js layer (both sendTextMessage and buildWhatsAppUrl) rather than at each call site
decisionLog.why: The bug had already independently drifted into a SECOND, duplicated, unnormalized implementation in shopController.js before this fix - clear evidence that leaving normalization as each caller's responsibility doesn't hold up over time. Centralizing it in the one shared service function it should have been in from the start prevents a third drift.

decisionLog.decision: Deferred the 'Target and Suggestion' monthly profit-goal feature after explaining the plan and asking a clarifying design question, per user instruction ('leave it fo now')
decisionLog.why: User asked to be told the implementation approach before building ('fist tell me how will you do it?'). After hearing the plan and a question about rule-based vs. AI-generated strategy text, the user chose to defer rather than decide - respected that as a stop, not a prompt to guess and proceed.

decisionLog.decision: Built bulk product import as an upsert (insert-or-update by SKU) rather than insert-only
decisionLog.why: User asked for 'bulk product import' generically; an insert-only design would force a separate bulk-update tool later for the very common case of re-importing the same supplier price list with updated costs/stock. Upsert covers both onboarding and ongoing catalog maintenance with one feature.

decisionLog.decision: Fixed .pos-cart-item's per-row auto-sized grid columns by switching to fixed pixel widths instead of trying to force consistent auto-sizing some other way (e.g. CSS Subgrid)
decisionLog.why: Each cart row renders as an independent DOM node/grid in this codebase's structure (no shared parent grid), so auto column widths are fundamentally computed per-row from that row's own content - fixed pixel widths are the simplest fix that guarantees identical column boundaries across rows regardless of price/name length, at the cost of the name column getting less space on a fixed 380px panel (addressed separately via 2-line text clamping).
